the following questions: (a) how should the receiver determine the rate at which it requests packets from the senders, given a certain level of packet loss and delay? (b) how should the packets be partitioned among the senders, in such a manner that the startup delay is minimized?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new receiver-driven video streaming protocol that is capable of streaming multiple video streams from multiple senders.
the proposed protocol achieves higher throughput and better performance than existing protocols in the presence of congestion, packet loss, and delay.

we have developed an effective, receiver-driven protocol for multiple sender distributed video streaming over best-effort networks, which can be used to improve video quality, reduce startup time and increase the number of users supported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multiple senders to stream video is an effective approach for improving performance in terms of both throughput and robustness to loss and delay.
the receiver-driven approach is effective in reducing packet loss, and that the receiver should take the lead in determining the sending rate for every sender.

, by employing multiple video senders to the same receiver and carefully allocating their sending rates, it is possible to achieve a substantial increase in the probability of successful packet delivery, and hence in video quality, without increasing bandwidth requirements or adding significant delay.
